title: The Classification of 3+1d Symmetry Enriched Topological Order: two-categorical (de-)equivariantization
author: Thibault D. Décoppet, Matthew Yu
work: The Classification of 3+1d Symmetry Enriched Topological Order
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem (source0.tex lines 745--747, source label thm:deequiv), the two-categorical (de-)equivariantization theorem: there is an equivalence of tricategories between braided fusion 2-categories containing the two-representations of the group fully faithfully and the group-crossed braided multifusion 2-categories with faithful grading; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 748--758 (one adjacent proof environment of 11 lines that opens and closes inside the retained span). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span: it identifies crossed braided multifusion 2-categories with rigid braided algebras in the Drinfeld centre of the tricategory of graded vector spaces, invokes the equivalence between that centre and the centre of the tricategory of two-representations of the group, transfers the classification of rigid braided algebras along that equivalence, and then verifies that the correspondence preserves the faithfulness of the grading, which is what remains to be shown. The theorem is the technical heart of the article's classification of symmetry enriched topological orders in three spatial dimensions, and its statement and proof are research-level. H2: a research-level higher-category-theory theorem whose proof combines the algebra-object description of crossed braided multifusion 2-categories, the Morita invariance of Drinfeld centres for fusion higher categories and a faithfulness check of the resulting correspondence; it is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
